title: Body & health
goal: Name parts of the body, say what hurts or what illness you have, understand a doctor's advice and say what someone should do.
intro: In Odia you don't say 'I have a headache' — you say *my head is aching* (ମୋ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି), *fever has happened to me* (ମୋର ଜ୍ୱର ହୋଇଛି) or *cold is striking me* (ମୋତେ ଥଣ୍ଡା ଲାଗୁଛି). This unit also introduces **ଉଚିତ** 'should'.

vocab.note: ମୋ ଦେହ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ 'I'm not well'.
You 'eat' medicine in Odia: ଔଷଧ ଖାଇବା.

phrases.en: I have a fever and a cough.

grammar.title: Saying what's wrong: experiencer constructions
grammar.body:
Odia describes illness in three typical ways:

1. **Body part + ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି** ('is aching') with a possessive: ମୋ **ମୁଣ୍ଡ** ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି 'my head aches', ତାଙ୍କ ପେଟ ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି 'his/her stomach aches'.
2. **Illness + ହୋଇଛି** ('has happened') with a possessive: ମୋର **ଜ୍ୱର** ହୋଇଛି 'I've got a fever'.
3. **Dative + feeling + ଲାଗୁଛି** ('is striking'): ମୋତେ **ଥଣ୍ଡା** ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel cold', ମୋତେ ବାନ୍ତି ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel sick'.

General health: ମୋ ଦେହ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ 'my body isn't well'. Accidents use compound verbs with **-ଗଲା** ('went'): ମୋ ହାତ କଟିଗଲା 'I cut my hand' (my hand got cut).

examples.en: The child has caught a chill.

grammar.title: 'Should': -ବା ଉଚିତ
grammar.body:
To say someone **should** do something, use the verbal noun (the dictionary form in **-ବା**) + **ଉଚିତ** 'proper'. The person goes in the possessive: ତୁମର ବିଶ୍ରାମ ନେବା ଉଚିତ — *your rest-taking [is] proper* — 'you should rest'. 'Shouldn't' is **ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ**.

Doctors usually just give polite commands: ଖାଆନ୍ତୁ 'take (eat)', ପିଅନ୍ତୁ 'drink', ନିଅନ୍ତୁ 'take'.

examples.native: ଏ ଔଷଧ ଦିନକୁ ତିନି ଥର ଖାଆନ୍ତୁ।
examples.roman: e ôusôdhô dinôku tini thôrô khaôntu.
examples.en: Take this medicine three times a day.

dialogue.title: At the clinic
dialogue.setting: Sam has been ill since yesterday and visits a local doctor.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Come in, sit down. What's happened?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଡାକ୍ତରବାବୁ, ଗତକାଲିଠାରୁ ମୋ ଦେହ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: ḍaktôrôbabu, gôtôkaliṭharu mo dehô bhôlô nahiṃ.
lines.en: Doctor, I haven't been well since yesterday.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୋର ଜ୍ୱର ହୋଇଛି, ଆଉ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ବହୁତ ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି।
lines.roman: morô jwôrô hoichhi, au muṇḍô bôhutô bindhuchhi.
lines.en: I've got a fever, and my head really aches.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Do you have a cough too?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଟିକିଏ କାଶ ଅଛି। ଗଳା ବି ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି।
lines.roman: ṭikie kasô ôchhi. gôḷa bi bindhuchhi.
lines.en: A bit of a cough. My throat hurts too.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ମୁହଁ ଖୋଲନ୍ତୁ। ହଁ, ଗଳା ନାଲି ହୋଇଛି। ଏହା ଭାଇରାଲ୍ ଜ୍ୱର।
lines.roman: muhôṃ kholôntu. hôṃ, gôḷa nali hoichhi. eha bhairal jwôrô.
lines.en: Open your mouth. Yes, your throat is red. It's a viral fever.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Nothing to worry about, is it?

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ନା। ଏ ଔଷଧ ଦିନକୁ ତିନି ଥର ଖାଆନ୍ତୁ, ଆଉ ବହୁତ ପାଣି ପିଅନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: na. e ôusôdhô dinôku tini thôrô khaôntu, au bôhutô paṇi piôntu.
lines.en: No. Take this medicine three times a day, and drink lots of water.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କର ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ବିଶ୍ରାମ ନେବା ଉଚିତ।
lines.roman: apôṇôṅkôrô dui dinô bisramô neba uchitô.
lines.en: You should rest for two days.

culture: Doctors are addressed respectfully as **ଡାକ୍ତରବାବୁ** (or ଡାକ୍ତର ଅପା for a woman). Pharmacies (ଔଷଧ ଦୋକାନ / medical store) are everywhere and pharmacists readily give advice for minor complaints. In the hot season (April–June), heatstroke (ଅଂଶୁଘାତ, *ôṅsughatô*) is a real danger: Odias drink *pakhala*, lassi, *bela pana* (wood-apple drink) and lots of water.

tip.title: Saying what hurts
tip.body:
- Aches: **my + body part + ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି**: ମୋ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି 'I have a headache'.
- Illnesses: **ମୋର + illness + ହୋଇଛି**: ମୋର ଜ୍ୱର ହୋଇଛି 'I've got a fever'.
- Feelings: **ମୋତେ + feeling + ଲାଗୁଛି**: ମୋତେ ଥଣ୍ଡା ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel cold'.
- In general: ମୋ **ଦେହ** ଭଲ ନାହିଁ 'I'm not well'.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଗଳା ବିନ୍ଧୁଛି, ଗରମ ପାଣି ଦିଅ।
sentences.roman: mo gôḷa bindhuchhi, gôrômô paṇi diô.
sentences.en: My throat hurts — give me some hot water. (familiar)

sentences.native: ଏବେ ମୋ ଦେହ ଟିକିଏ ଭଲ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: ebe mo dehô ṭikie bhôlô ôchhi.
sentences.en: I'm feeling a bit better now.
The child has a lovely face.

tip.title: Hand or arm? Leg or foot?
tip.body:
- **ହାତ** = hand *and* arm; **ଗୋଡ଼** = leg *and* foot.
- Accidents use a verb + **-ଗଲା** 'went': ମୋ ହାତ **କଟିଗଲା** 'I've cut my hand', ତାଙ୍କ ଗୋଡ଼ **ଭାଙ୍ଗିଗଲା** 'he/she broke a leg'.
- Where it hurts: body part + **-ରେ** + ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣା ହେଉଛି: ଛାତିରେ ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣା ହେଉଛି.

sentences.en: I've got a pain in my chest.

sentences.native: ଆଘାତ ବେଶି ନୁହେଁ, ଚିନ୍ତା କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: aghatô besi nuheṃ, chinta kôrôntu nahiṃ.
sentences.en: The injury isn't bad — don't worry.

tip.title: Illnesses "happen" to you
tip.body:
- Illnesses have happened to you: **ମୋର** ଜ୍ୱର **ହୋଇଛି** 'I've got a fever', ତାଙ୍କର ସର୍ଦ୍ଦି ହୋଇଛି.
- Nausea is a feeling: **ମୋତେ** ବାନ୍ତି **ଲାଗୁଛି** 'I feel sick'.
- Lasting conditions use ଅଛି: ମୋର ଆଲର୍ଜି ଅଛି.
- **ଅସୁସ୍ଥ** = ill: ସେ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ଅଛନ୍ତି.

sentences.en: The child has diarrhoea and vomiting.

sentences.native: ଜ୍ୱର ନାହିଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଟିକିଏ କାଶ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: jwôrô nahiṃ, kintu ṭikie kasô ôchhi.
sentences.en: No fever, but a bit of a cough.

tip.title: 'Should': -ବା ଉଚିତ
tip.body:
- Dictionary form (-ବା) + **ଉଚିତ**: ତୁମର ବିଶ୍ରାମ ନେବା ଉଚିତ 'you should rest'.
- The person takes the 'of' form: ମୋର, ତୁମର, ଆପଣଙ୍କର.
- 'Shouldn't': **ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ**.
- Doctors mostly give polite commands: ଔଷଧ **ଖାଆନ୍ତୁ** 'take the medicine' — in Odia you *eat* medicine.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କର ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ଘରେ ରହିବା ଉଚିତ।
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkôrô dui dinô ghôre rôhiba uchitô.
sentences.en: You should stay at home for two days.
You shouldn't eat curd at night.

sentences.native: ଏ ଔଷଧ ସକାଳେ ଆଉ ରାତିରେ ଖାଆନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: e ôusôdhô sôkaḷe au ratire khaôntu.
sentences.en: Take this medicine morning and night.
When does the doctor see patients?
